title: Composable multi-satellite precipitation estimation for evolving observing systems
abstract: arXiv:2605.14426v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Rapid and spatially continuous precipitation monitoring is critical for flood, landslide, and other hydrometeorological hazard warnings, particularly in regions where rain-gauge and weather-radar networks are sparse. The coordinated use of heterogeneous satellite observations, including geostationary infrared, passive microwave, and spaceborne radar measurements, is therefore a key pathway toward more accurate and spatially refined precipitation monitoring. Recent deep-learning methods have substantially improved multi-source satellite precipitation estimation, but most remain tied to predefined combinations of satellite inputs. As satellite observing systems evolve, incorporating new instruments often requires substantial model retraining and maintenance. translated_title: 面向演进观测系统的可组合多卫星降水估计
translated_abstract: 快速且空间连续的降水监测对于洪水、滑坡及其他水文气象灾害预警至关重要，尤其是在雨量计和天气雷达网络稀疏的地区。因此，协同利用包括静止轨道红外、被动微波和星载雷达测量在内的异构卫星观测，是实现更精确、空间上更精细降水监测的关键途径。近期的深度学习方法显著提升了多源卫星降水估计的精度，但大多数方法仍受限于预定义的卫星输入组合。随着卫星观测系统的不断演进，纳入新仪器往往需要对模型进行大量的再训练和维护。我们提出了PRISMA，一个用于多源观测降水反演的生成式框架。该框架将降水先验的训练与传……
tldr: 提出PRISMA生成式框架，将降水先验训练与传感器建模解耦，使多源卫星降水估计能够灵活适应不断演进的卫星观测系统，无需大规模再训练即可纳入新仪器。
en_tdlr: We propose PRISMA, a generative framework that decouples precipitation prior training from sensor modeling, enabling composable multi-satellite precipitation estimation that flexibly adapts to evolving observing systems without extensive retraining.
